newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says U.S. pork imports restricted by taste.
newsitem.headline: Manila says U.S. pork imports restricted by taste.

text.p: The Philippines, responding to U.S complaints over pork sales, said on Tuesday imports from the United States were restricted because Filipinos did not like the taste of frozen pork.
"We are not restricting them," Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero told Reuters when asked for a comment on the U.S. complaint. He was in Bacolod for a conference of sugar farmers.
The lower sales of U.S. pork in the Philippines was "largely because of resistance of consumers here. Filipinos are not used to frozen pork," he said.
U.S. Trade Representative-designate Charlene Barshefsky said in Washington on Monday the United States would file a complaint against the Philippines at the World Trade Organisation over pork sales.
Escudero said he told the U.S. Embassy in Manila last week that there were no pending applications for pork imports.
In December last year, Escudero told Reuters the Philippines will increase the amount of frozen pork imports it will allow into the country to as much as 53,000 tonnes.
Manila had allowed pork imports of up to 49,900 tonnes in 1996 but Philippine livestock companies imported only about 2,500 tonnes.
Officials said the imports were low because most consumers preferred fresh pork.
